articles.title: Every Fire Emblem Game on the Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 in 2026
articles.summary: The Nintendo Switch is home to five games from the tactical RPG series Fire Emblem. Here's the full list.
articles.body:
It’s been 36 years since Intelligent Systems debuted its Fire Emblem series on Nintendo's Famicom. Through its ever-evolving combat and the introduction of beloved character bonding mechanics, the series has ascended to the upper echelon of tactical RPGs , culminating in two excellent mainline entries on the Nintendo Switch.

Now that we have Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave has officially arrived, we’ve compiled a list of every Fire Emblem game available on the Switch as well as what's coming to the Switch 2.

How Many Fire Emblem Games Are on Switch?

There are six Fire Emblem games on Switch: three mainline games and three spinoffs. There are three additional Fire Emblem games available with Nintendo Switch Online, though Path of Radiance is only available to Switch 2 owners with the Expansion Pack.

Every Fire Emblem Game on Nintendo Switch

The first Fire Emblem game released on Switch was the Dynasty Warriors crossover Fire Emblem Warriors . The mashup incorporates the best elements of each series, blending Fire Emblem’s team-based strategy with Dynasty Warriors’ button-mashing, hack-and-slash action. It’s a worthwhile spinoff for action fans, though the light story makes it inessential to those concerned with Fire Emblem lore.

The game was developed by Dynasty Warriors studio Omega Force in collaboration with the action gurus at Team Ninja (Ninja Gaiden, Nioh).

Fire Emblem: Three Houses was a milestone release for the series. It was the first Fire Emblem game released on a home console in 12 years, the first mainline entry released on Switch, and a critical and commercial success that carried forward the momentum of Awakening seven years before it.

Three Houses is a massive tactical RPG that balances the grand with the intimate. Large-scale battles progress an overarching story of politics and religion within a continental war, while quieter moments between battles are spent in the monastery training, teaching, exploring, and bonding with other characters through well-written and -acted conversations.

Three Houses is Fire Emblem at its best, and what we'd recommend as a starting point if you’re looking to jump into the series on Switch.

In 2020, Nintendo released Tokyo Mirage Sessions #FE Encore, an expanded port of the original Wii U release. Encore added new story content, characters, and music to the Nintendo-Atlus crossover game, which blends Fire Emblem’s “weapon triangle” combat mechanic — swords have an advantage over axes, axes over lances, lances over swords — with the flashy style, dungeon-crawling, and moment-to-moment combat of Atlus’s Shin Megami Tensei and Persona games .

The story is a comical, often over-the-top send-up of Japanese pop-culture that, as in Warriors before it, takes a backseat to the action.

Fire Emblem Warriors: Three Hopes (2023)

Nintendo re-teamed with Omega Force for Fire Emblem Warriors: Three Hopes , the companies’ second Fire Emblem-Dynasty Warriors crossover following Fire Emblem Warriors. Three Hopes is a retelling of Three Houses set in an alternate timeline where Three Houses’ protagonist Byleth serves as the main villain.

Three Hopes is a more robust blend of the two franchises than its predecessor, integrating more of Fire Emblem’s social and tactical mechanics with Dynasty Warriors’ fast-paced action.

Fire Emblem Engage is the series’ latest game and its second mainline entry on Switch. Engage is a progression of Three Houses’ excellence and an ode to Fire Emblem's past: It refines and scales down the social and hub mechanics of Three Houses while shifting its primary focus to the series’ longstanding tactical combat, most notably reintroducing Fire Emblem’s “weapon triangle" system.

The story of Engage follows a Divine Dragon named Alear, who’s tasked with collecting 12 rings to defeat the Fell Dragon and save the continent of Elyos. Engage’s original story connects to the series past through these 12 rings, each of which houses the spirit of a past Fire Emblem protagonist, allowing you to summon past heroes such as Marth, Ike, Celica, and Byleth.

Fire Emblem: Fortunes Weave is the first game from the franchise to be released on the Switch 2. It's also shaping up to be one of the best Fire Emblem games ever made. IGN gave the game a perfect 10 out of 10 in our review , saying it: "provides an excellent pairing of combat strategy and management, with compelling stories spread across each of its four heroes that come together to form one phenomenal RPG."

Fire Emblem Games Available With Nintendo Switch Online

Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack: 12-Month Individual Membership

There are currently three Fire Emblem games available with a Nintendo Switch Online subscription outside of Japan: the 2003 Game Boy Advance game Fire Emblem, aka Fire Emblem: The Blazing Blade, and the 2004 follow-up Fire Emblem: The Sacred Stones. A third game, 2005's Fire Emblem: Path of Radiance, was also added to the catalog when GameCube games launched on the Switch 2.

Here’s the complete list of Fire Emblem games currently available with a Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack subscription:

Upcoming Fire Emblem Games on Switch and Switch 2

With the release of Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave on the Switch 2, we don't yet have any information about the next game in the series. The most recent Nintendo Direct did not feature any mention of the franchise, so we probably won't heare more until 2027 about what's coming next.

Jordan covers games, shows, and movies as a freelance writer for IGN.

articles.title: My Cat Scattered Games: Tidy Videogame Supermarket Announced for PC
articles.summary: If you're a gamer who likes organizing your physical collection and you're looking for a new cozy game to play, indie developer ODIUS and publisher Loopr Partners's My Cat Scattered Games: Tidy Videogame Supermarket might be exactly what you want. Bonus points if you like cats. My Cat Scattered Games is a literal title: your in-game cat has taken your gargantuan physical games collection (represented here as funny, legally distinct versions of their real-life counterparts) and, as cats do, scattered them all over your the place. It's up to you to pick them all up and reorganize them on your shelves.
articles.body:
If you're a gamer who likes organizing your physical collection and you're looking for a new cozy game to play, indie developer ODIUS and publisher Loopr Partners's My Cat Scattered Games: Tidy Videogame Supermarket might be exactly what you want. Bonus points if you like cats. My Cat Scattered Games is a literal title: your in-game cat has taken your gargantuan physical games collection (represented here as funny, legally distinct versions of their real-life counterparts) and, as cats do, scattered them all over your the place. It's up to you to pick them all up and reorganize them on your shelves.

You can organize over 6,000 games and consoles such as "Lovable Kombat," "Mega Bavario 64," and "Red Spirit 2" for systems like the "Kekstation 2" and "Y-box." You'll also need to rescue your cat, who after making this mess, somehow got itself trapped in a claw machine. Check out the first trailer above and the first screenshots in the gallery below.

My Cat Scattered Games: Tidy Videogame Supermarket - First Screenshots

"The job sounds simple enough," the developer says. "Pick up a game, identify its platform, find the right section, and put it back on the shelf. But with thousands of discs, cartridges, consoles, and other gaming treasures scattered across the store, keeping everything organized is easier said than done. Each shelf can hold up to three different games and ten copies of each title, giving players plenty of room to develop their own sorting strategy. As the store gradually comes back together, players can discover parody game covers, jokes, and references inspired by different eras of video game history."

You'll unlock ways to speed up your sorting and organization as you progress, but there are no ways to fail the game or lose. It's completely cozy and go-at-your-own-pace. [ Editor's Note: It's almost like this was built for me and my mild OCD.] My Cat Scattered Games will be released for PC on October 9, and you can wishlist it on Steam if you're interested.

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked , and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch . He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .

articles.title: Valor Mortis Costs $40 Because of 'The Craziest Fall in the History of This Business'
articles.summary: Promising first-person action soulslike Valor Mortis has a confirmed $40 price point, which was settled upon by its publisher because of the fall crush fueled by GTA 6.
articles.body:
Promising first-person action soulslike Valor Mortis has a confirmed $40 price point, which was settled upon by its publisher because of the fall crush fueled by GTA 6.

“We have had many discussions over the past year about the price of Valor Mortis,” publisher Lyrical Games said in a statement. “We believe the game has the quality, fidelity, and playtime in its 20-hour story to go toe-to-toe with many ‘full-price’ titles. Still, this Fall is stacked and there’s high demand for your time and money.”

Valor Mortis was already delayed from September 24 to October 13 to avoid the likes of Remedy’s Control Resonant and Konami’s Silent Hill: Townfall, but it also faces the looming launch of GTA 6 a month later. The hope is that by going with a cheaper price than some of its competitors it’ll stand out further, but what comes with that is the risk that some will feel it’s not as good.

In an interview with The Game Business , Lyrical Games boss Blake Rochkind expanded on the decision, admitting the price was something “we’ve really agonized over.”

“My biggest concern was that it would send the wrong message about the game. But this decision is made out of confidence,” he said.

“We find ourselves as one of the only new IPs launching in what is objectively the craziest fall in the history of this business. Not only do you have GTA looming large in November, now you have the Zelda remake, Control coming out in a couple of weeks, Silent Hill: Townfall, Phantom Blade Zero, Gears of War, Call of Duty... By virtue of the development schedule, the cards we’ve been dealt is that we are one of the only new IPs launching this fall.

“We are pretty confident in Valor Mortis. But ultimately, the worst thing we could do is not push our chips in and say, ‘We want this to be a game that you can pick up alongside these other great games.’”

This latter point is that Valor Mortis could be a game people buy as well as another, perhaps more expensive game, and a $40 price point makes that decision easier. Perhaps someone plans to buy GTA 6, which at its cheapest costs $80, but wouldn't mind snapping up Valor Mortis at half the price to play in the weeks beforehand.

Or maybe they will play Control Resonant and also Valor Mortis, or any other combination. “Going with this price point will help us be an ‘and’ game,” Rochkind said.

It’s worth noting that Valor Mortis is a day one Xbox Game Pass release, although Rochkind insisted this had nothing to do with the pricing decision.

From the creators of Ghostrunner, Valor Mortis is a first-person soulslike where you rise from death as a former soldier of Napoleon’s army, only to die over and over again battling shambling corpses and wild monsters. You can get a rundown on Valor Mortis in our recent preview.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

articles.title: Metroid Prime 4: Beyond On Switch Drops to $35 During Nintendo’s Customer Appreciation Sale
articles.summary: Metroid Prime 4: Beyond on Nintendo Switch is 42% off at both Amazon and Best Buy, dropping to $34.99, as part of Nintendo's Customer Appreciation Sale.
articles.body:
Nintendo's new Customer Appreciation Sale is full of game deals to look through, including some nice finds for Metroid fans. While Metroid Dread is one that's caught our eye in the sale (a perfect pick-up before Metroid Ravenous drops next year), the physical copy of Metroid Prime 4: Beyond on the original Switch is also on sale at both Amazon and Best Buy with a huge 42% discount.

This price cut has brought it down to just $34.99 (you'll get the deal price at Best Buy after adding it to your cart), which is $25 cheaper compared to paying full price for it. That's a nice little chunk of cash to save, and not terribly far away from its lowest price point at Amazon of $29.99, either.

Metroid Prime 4: Beyond - Nintendo Switch

Not to mention, it's a great deal to go with if you're hoping to grab it for Switch 2. Considering the Switch 2 Edition Upgrade Pack is priced at $10, it would bring the grand total up to $45 when paired with this deal, which beats the standard Switch 2 copy's list price of $69.99 (and even Amazon's current sale price of $50.99 ).

If you decide to pick it up, you're in for a treat. Metroid Prime 4: Beyond was one of our top reviewed games of 2025 , earning a glowing 8/10 review score. IGN's Logan Plant called it "an excellent, if relatively uneven, revival that reaches heights worthy of the Metroid name in its best moments." And with Metroid Ravenous due out next year , it's a perfect time to jump back into some of the other games.

There's plenty more where Metroid Prime 4: Beyond came from, too. Nintendo's Customer Appreciation Sale is still going strong until September 26 , offering a wide variety of discounts on games, accessories, amiibo, and more.

If you're looking to grab some goodies for the Nintendo fan in your life before the holiday season, this is a great opportunity to shop around. We may not see a lot of these offers again until Black Friday and Cyber Monday , either, so it's as good a time as any to buy.

Hannah Hoolihan is a freelancer who writes with the commerce team here at IGN.

articles.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker’s Hunger Is a Dark Urge to Match Baldur’s Gate 3
articles.summary: The Blood of Dawnwalker’s vampiric hunger system has turned me into a serial NPC killer, and it's like Baldur's Gate 3's Dark Urge all over again.
articles.body:
This is an IGN opinion piece from Matt Purslow, who loves RPGs both on the tabletop and in video game form. He appreciates any game that has an interesting take on the evil within, probably because his first ever RPG character was the son of the god of murder.

My sword slices through the final soldier. As his body hits the forest floor, my work here is done: I have saved two innocent men from being marched to the draining camps. Ambrus, the vampire that rules over this region of Vale Sangora, is rounding up civilians and bottling their blood to create a stockpile of sustenance. It’s my job to disrupt all that, and this latest round of vigilante slaughter is part of that task. These men will not be drained today.

You see, I’ve made the poor decision of conducting this mission at night. When the moon rises, I become a vampire myself, and while that grants me a suite of helpful abilities, such as being able to turn into a wolf and walk up walls, it also means I need to feast on blood. And, well, after all that slaughter, I’m pretty hungry.

As the two men thank me for my heroics, my regular dialogue choices are replaced with “Give in to the hunger.” I resist, choosing the only option that will push forward the conversation. One of the men promises to give me a suitable reward for saving his life. All my response options have been overridden by the hunger. I refuse to select one. The fangs come out anyway. So much for saving these men from being drained.

In The Blood of Dawnwalker, being a vampire truly is a curse. Protagonist Coen is sired in the story’s early hours, but it’s an imperfect transformation; during the day he remains a human, but at night the vampirism takes over. Regular health-restoring items like food and water become impossible to palette, and so only blood can repair his wounds. But the red stuff isn’t just a nice-to-have; it’s a necessity. An addiction. And so if you let Coen’s HP linger in the bottom section of his health bar, where it flashes like a warning beacon, you risk the hunger taking over. When you enter conversations, dialogue options are replaced by “Give in to the hunger.” Resist too long, and Coen will chow down on whoever is in front of him… regardless of how important they are to the plot. Yes, you can accidentally kill anyone and everyone , from random civilians to major quest-giving NPCs. Never before has it been so important to keep your belly full.

Coen is far from the only “monster” protagonist in RPGs. Obsidian Entertainment is fascinated by the idea, allowing you to murder most NPCs in its The Outer Worlds duology and Fallout: New Vegas, as well as building an entire campaign around the idea of evil in Tyranny. But Coen feels like an interesting reflection of the Dark Urge, Baldur’s Gate 3’s optional origin story that casts you as a depraved serial killer. As the Dark Urge, you’re given additional layers of choice that allow you to revel in your grisly nature – the most famous of which is probably being able to tear off the hand of wizard Gale when you first meet him, killing the potential companion before he can be recruited.

Like Baldur’s Gate 3’s most sinister origin, Coen quite literally has a dark urge that pushes him to do unspeakable things. But while these characters are reflections of each other, their symmetry is warped. Coen’s urge is systemic – there are conditions that, when met, will trigger his uncontrollable hunger, which can disrupt the decisions you’ve made. The Dark Urge, meanwhile, layers additional choices into Baldur’s Gate 3 that allow you to author your own story of a serial killer navigating the tentacled apocalypse. These two approaches to choice create two very different takes on a similar idea.

With the Dark Urge, it’s all about crafting your character’s journey. Throughout the course of the story, a Dark Urge player is presented with many, many additional dialogue options and scenarios that allow them to engage with more sinister ideas than those presented to the more “traditional” Baldur’s Gate player characters. During the first act, for instance, the Dark Urge is given the opportunity to mutilate animals, break the legs of a refugee, bite off a goblin’s toe, brutally murder a companion following a steamy nocturnal engagement, and butcher one of the game’s most beloved NPCs.

By presenting these as options, rather than uncontrollable desires, each becomes a story branch that you choose to enact, which in turn allows you to shape the Dark Urge’s personality. Perhaps your version of this character has a code, like the titular serial killer of the AMC show Dexter, and will only murder a particular kind of personality. Maybe they’re an animal lover and will refrain from plucking the wings off injured birds. And then there’s what’s widely considered the most satisfying manner in which to play the Dark Urge: the redemption arc, in which you wrestle with your inner darkness and try to become the hero that the Sword Coast needs.

To make that redemption arc feel authentic, there does need to be some systemic elements that ensure your urges are just beyond your control, and so there are a few moments where you must pass a skill check dice roll in order to suppress your murderous intent. But for the most part, the experience of the Dark Urge is about writing your own destiny – how will your choices define your murderer?

The Blood of Dawnwalker - IGN First Exclusive Images

There is, of course, crossover between Baldur’s Gate 3’s Dark Urge and The Blood of Dawnwalker. As Coen, there are several opportunities to tread a purposefully grisly path, and your dialogue choices will dictate the kind of man he becomes. But as my accidental feast demonstrates, controlling Coen’s dark urge is more about mastering Dawnwalker’s systems. It’s vital to understand how his hunger works, as that understanding allows you to make informed gameplay decisions that can keep that hunger in check.

For instance, a reasonably early quest tasked me with breaking into a jail to rescue the local miller. After scoping out the small castle during the day, I gathered enough intelligence to understand that this prison break was best conducted at night, as there would be fewer guards. And so after dark I used my vampiric powers to teleport over the fence, pilfered the cell key, and freed my quarry. However, fewer guards doesn’t mean no guards at all, and so I was forced to spill some blood on my way out – Dawnwalker unfortunately doesn’t feature any genuine stealth systems, and so even the sneakiest plans typically require some direct confrontation.

The battle left my health bar in the flashing red, and so when it came to the quest’s final conversation with the prisoner before he was free to leave, my dialogue options began to shudder, replaced by that ominous “Give in to the hunger.” The sudden panic this induces is deeply effective – unlike the men I’d accidentally drained earlier, this prisoner was a more significant character in the story. I really didn’t want to eat him. Suddenly, I was re-thinking all my choices – why didn’t I drink a blood vial before talking with the prisoner? Was there a way out that didn’t involve combat? Why didn’t I do this quest in the day, when there’s no risk of hunger?

Luckily, fate was on my side this time – the prisoner thanked me and escaped without my fangs puncturing his neck. But it could have been a very different story. And that’s the beauty of Dawnwalker’s systemic approach to hunger. It’s not just a health replenishment system; it’s a very real curse that demands you properly consider the risks of working through the night. Of course, it’s not just as simple as opting to play solely during the day – the game’s most famous feature is the 30-day countdown until your family dies, and so this exerts pressure on you to use time wisely. Do you really want to avoid the night when so much could be achieved in those hours? After all, it’s the only time when you can use your powerful suite of vampiric abilities.

Your choice here isn’t just about mitigating a gameplay risk, though. It’s also about writing Coen’s story. If you try to avoid your curse – if you sleep during the night, or restrict yourself to nighttime quests that don’t involve NPCs you want to keep alive – you’re creating a particular version of Coen. Does he fear who he’s become? Does he hate himself? Or is he deeply caring of everyone, so much so he’ll risk running out of time to save his family to ensure the other residents of Vale Sangora are kept safe from his hunger? How you respond to this gameplay challenge helps define the story you extract from The Blood of Dawnwalker. It’s another fascinating layer to a game that’s already doing plenty with its time system and “narrative sandbox” to ensure everyone’s playthrough is unique .

Baldur’s Gate 3 and The Blood of Dawnwalker are, of course, very different RPGs with many distinct approaches to handling choice, consequence, and storytelling. The rich reactivity of Baldur’s Gate 3 is often the result of several libraries’ worth of authored narrative branches, allowing for as close an approximation of the tabletop Dungeons & Dragons experience as possible. Dawnwalker is also inspired by the freedom of tabletop RPGs, but its approach is somewhat more systemic in nature, allowing the gears of the game’s systems to dictate the story’s flow as much as pre-written choices. The end result is an experience that functions differently, but – at least in the case of its examination of the vampire curse and the burden it inflicts – easily evokes the same thrills as one of Baldur’s Gate 3’s best ideas.

Matt Purslow is IGN's Executive Editor of Features.

articles.title: Explosive Elon Musk Documentary Likely to Be Dropped by Universal, Report Claims
articles.summary: Universal is reportedly reconsidering its release of a revealing Elon Musk documentary, despite it receiving rave reviews at recent film festivals.
articles.body:
Universal is reportedly reconsidering its release of a revealing Elon Musk documentary, despite it receiving rave reviews at recent film festivals.

Weighing in at four hours (with a 10-minute intermission), Musk is the work of prolific filmmaker Alex Gibney, who secured access to various figures close to the Grok owner in his personal life, as well as those who comment on his political influence.

But while an informative documentary on the world's richest man would likely put bums on seats, The Hollywood Reporter claims that Universal is now likely to drop the movie's full release.

Universal paid millions for the rights to release Musk back in 2023, before the now-trillionaire fully aligned himself with President Donald Trump. Today, however, there's reportedly hesitancy over launching the film, with the expected outcome now that the movie rights will be returned to Gibney for him to sell again elsewhere.

In a thread on Twitter/X, which Musk owns, former Wall Street Journal and NBC News journalist Matt Rivera recounted watching the documentary at Venice Film Festival, where it received a five-minute ovation, and listed an array of eye-opening details regarding the film's contents.

These includes purported claims by Musk's former partner Ashley St. Clair that the trillionaire knew the 2024 election result hours before it was made official due to "lasers in space." The movie also includes Musk's reaction to the Wall Street Journal's reporting of his alleged drug use, and discussion of the NDA that St. Clair claims she was asked to sign after giving birth to one of Musk's 14 known children.

The "lasers in space" claim previously caught the eye of Musk's attorney Alex Spiro, who appeared to debunk the phrase having any other meaning than a reference to how Starlink satellites communicate in space. In a letter to Gibney and the film's producers at Jigsaw Productions, reported by NPR , Spiro stated that the filmmaker had been put "on notice."

"Starlink was not connected to vote tabulation," Spiro wrote. "Election officials in multiple states, independent cybersecurity researchers, and fact-checkers publicly refuted the Starlink vote-rigging claim in November 2024, and nothing since has revived it. Starlink's satellites communicate by laser inter-satellite link; that is what 'lasers in space' describes. You are therefore on notice, before release, that the insinuation is false, that the material refuting it is public, and that you chose not to be told the rest."

In response, Jigsaw stated that it had a "right to engage in open debate and fact-based examinations of powerful public figures" protected by the First Amendment, "something that should be recognized and defended by all Americans, including the associates of Elon Musk, who has proclaimed himself to be a 'free speech absolutist.'"

Other former partners and family members of Musk also feature in the documentary, though Musk (perhaps unsurprisingly) declined to take part. Instead, re-enactments of his public comments are made by a CGI replacement as a "literal staging of the film's theme," Rivera wrote, "a man who manufactures his reality."

Musk has recently fired off a string of social media posts regarding the movie, dubbing it as a "hit piece that misses" and "a false film" that was also "boring." Neither Musk or Spiro have seen the film, and the two sides have clashed over Gibney's refusal to discuss its material with them, while Gibney has stated that Musk refused to take part and be interviewed.

"This isn't the hit job Musk claims," Rivera concluded, after watching the movie. "At times, it bends over backward to be fair. But it pierces Musk's mythos, playing some stories twice to expose contradictions and posing open questions: What's with all the kids? What is he doing with all that data?"

Universal ditching Musk would not be the only recent example of a distributor dropping a documentary that could make for uncomfortable viewing. Amazon previously walked away from the Sam Altman documentary Artificial, days after signing a $50 billion deal with Altman's company OpenAI. Musk was also featured in that film, which will now see its release via indie distributor Neon.

The Hollywood Reporter also highlights the current situation with Musk's streaming release, which HBO has paid for (and also contributed further funds to the film's budget when needed during filming). HBO will likely soon be owned by Warner Bros., in a deal backed by CEO David Ellison and his billionaire father Larry. Musk reportedly features Larry Ellison in an unfavorable light — so it will be interesting to see if the documentary's streaming launch goes ahead as planned, too.

Image credit: Benjamin Fanjoy/Getty Images.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: Brandon Sanderson Pushes Back on Suggestions He Could Finish George R.R. Martin’s Game of Thrones Books
articles.summary: "George doesn't owe people books..." — In an exclusive interview with IGN, Brandon Sanderson explains why he would refuse to finish George R.R. Martin's A Song of Ice and Fire series if asked, urging fans to offer support and patience to Martin instead.
articles.body:
In a recent interview with IGN, Brandon Sanderson said he would refuse any offers to continue George R.R. Martin's A Song of Ice and Fire series if the author dies before completing Winds of Winter (or the book after that).

Asked whether he would consider finishing the series, as he did with Wheel of Time , Sanderson said:

"Respectfully, I'm the wrong person to do this – and I think most fans of both of our works would agree. My entire career is, in a way, a response to A Song of Ice and Fire. Much as that series is a response to popular fiction of the 1990s, like Wheel of Time.

"If I were to say yes, I would do my best to write it exactly as fans want and expect, but I would not say yes – because there are much more natural fits out there, and if George decided to go that direction, he'd deserve someone who is as good a fit for his world as I was for Wheel of Time. That said, I don't think George wants to go that direction, so let's just support him in writing his books at the speed he's capable of going."

This tracks with what George R.R. Martin has said this year , stating that there's no plan for anyone else to step in. Instead, his Song of Ice and Fire series simply "won't be finished."

The 77 year old also recently acknowledged the lack of updates regarding the famous book series and described the year so far as having been "stressful, to say the least."

"So much has been happening, it's been overwhelming," Martin wrote in a post titled 'Better Late Than Never.' "Some great things, exciting things. Dreams coming true. But there have been nightmares too. I have lost friends. Battled sadness and depression. The worst may be yet to come."

"I turned 77 last September, and I tell you, getting old is no fun," Martin continued. "But there have been amazing times as well."

When chatting to IGN, Sanderson also reflected on Martin's recent challenges with mental health: "I implore people, in this discussion, to remember the person."

"George R. R. Martin is one of the greats of our genre, and in my every interaction with him, he's treated me with kindness – even when I was a nobody. He truly is the great patriarch of the fantasy genre, and has done a great deal of work fostering new talent, helping the community, and offering advice and support when needed."

Sanderson followed up, saying: "At the same time, writing can be a lonely profession, and we all know the difficulty of a book that just WILL NOT work. I've been fortunate that books like that have always been side projects for me, ones I can abandon without it causing too many ripples in my career. The only thing that will lead to A Song of Ice and Fire being finished is our support, patience, and effort to remember what makes books special: the fact that they are one of the few mass media art forms that are still largely created by individual human beings."

Martin has also repeatedly suggested frustration over discussions of his health at convention panels, and said he was aware of the online speculation around his age and health. "They say, 'He lied to us, he is going to die soon, look how old he is.' I really didn’t need that shit,” he said, referring to the fan question. "Nobody needs that shit."

When discussing Martin, Sanderson continued to push back against the idea that authors "owe" their audience a finished saga: "George doesn't owe people books, as he cannot actually make that promise – none of us can."

8 Shows to Watch if You Liked Game of Thrones

"I can't promise the end of the Stormlight Archive , because who knows if I'll come down with a sickness tomorrow. I am literally incapable of making promises about the future in that way, the same as any person is. That said, I do think we, as authors, are making a contract with readers when we start a book series – and that contract implies a certain responsibility on our part. The promise to work on the project, to give it due attention, to try our best to get the books done in a timely way. However, this is an art.

"I am as guilty as anyone of, now and then, making light of the fact that we don't have a conclusion to Game of Thrones. However, I live in a glass house, as I have a book ( The Rithmatist ) that I've promised fans a sequel to for as long as people have been waiting for George's next volume. I feel terrible I haven't been able to deliver, but the artistic process can be a whimsical one."

Sanderson finished by saying: "Regardless, I don't know that George owes anyone books as much as he owes them real, dedicated effort in producing those books, which might seem like semantics, but I'm an author. That's the job. It's not, however, my job to determine if George has made that effort or not. My gut says that he has – and the fact that we're where we are indicates that this is one of those times when the rest of the world has to wrestle with a terrible fact we as authors face every day. That from the outside, this seems like a trade (like making cabinets) when in reality it's an art, much like making music… and sometimes, you lose that music. [Let's] just hope it's not forever."

Like all of Sanderson's ongoing projects, you can track progress directly on his website where he has percentage bars for everything he's working on right now, including the Mistborn screenplay , Songrise 4.0, Ghostbloods Book 1 Draft 2.0, and Riftwake Book 3.

You can read more of the big Brandon Sanderson interview here on IGN, where we've discussed last year's Wheel of Time cancellation, potential video game adaptations of his work, and progress on the Mistborn movie.

articles.title: MTG Marvel Sets: 4 Crossover Predictions for 2027 and Beyond
articles.summary: Explore our predictions for upcoming MTG Marvel sets, including Guardians of the Galaxy, X-Men, Midnight Sons, and Secret Wars.
articles.body:
Magic: The Gathering has shown it’s happy to return to planes within the confines of its own universe, but the game’s Universes Beyond sets with Marvel are really only getting started.

Last year’s underwhelming Spider-Man set was followed up by the much more impressive Marvel Super Heroes set in 2026, but we’re expecting many more to come. After two Infinity Stones appeared in those sets, we’re still waiting for another four of them to appear.

Here are our Marvel set predictions for 2027 and beyond. Looking for our wider Universes Beyond predictions? Check out our ideas so far .

Conspicuous by their absence in the Marvel Super Heroes set are the Guardians of the Galaxy, but given it’s predominantly centered around New York City it’s perhaps not too surprising.

Star-Lord, Gamora, Drax, Rocket, and Groot feel like they could helm a five-color Commander deck, but beyond that, there’s a whole host of cosmic characters we could see.

Beta Ray Bill, Ronan, Gladiator, Nova, Adam Warlock, Nebula, and many more would be great inclusions, but it would also allow for extra printings of Galactus, Silver Surfer, and more. Given Star Trek is coming soon, and Edge of Eternities introduced Spacecraft, expect a card for The Milano.

Yes, we know - some X-Men have been included in the Marvel Super Heroes set, but it’s time for a wider slate of mutants from Xavier’s school and Magneto’s Brotherhood.

It’s likely cards like Wolverine and Storm would see reprints (and maybe fresh designs), but a two-faced card with Jean Grey and the Dark Phoenix, or saga cards for Days of Future Past and more would be awesome.

We’ll take a few more, too, since the likes of Deadpool have been included in Secret Lair drops but aren’t part of the Marvel set. Oh, and Gambit, please, but with an ability that lets you ping a card at your opponent.

Marvel has long had a spooky side, and while the Midnight Suns video game remains an underrated gem, the source team, The Midnight Sons, would be an awesome inclusion in Magic form.

Blade, Morbius, Ghost Riders, Man-Thing, Elsa Bloodstone, and even Doctor Strange and Wong could make appearances, and the main roster has included the likes of Scarlet Spider, Iron Fist, and many, many more.

That gives a chance to bring back the horror theming of, say, Duskmourn, reviving mechanics like manifest dread.

This could also be another major story moment, but an event set around Secret Wars, which is expected to be the focus of the next big tentpole MCU movie after Doomsday, feels like a given.

The set could include just about anyone transported to Battleworld, teeing up iconic moments that we won’t spoil here in case you’ve not read up on the source material yet.

Secret Wars would be a fitting endcap to the Marvel x MtG crossovers, and you just know we’d get some kind of crazy rare God Emperor Doom card…

What are your predictions? Let us know in the comments!

Lloyd Coombes is an experienced freelancer in tech, gaming and fitness seen at Polygon, Eurogamer, Macworld, TechRadar and many more. He's a big fan of Magic: The Gathering and other collectible card games, much to his wife's dismay.

articles.title: GTA Online Will Be Supported 'Beyond' GTA 6 Release, PC 'Becoming More and More Important'
articles.summary: Rockstar Games plans to support GTA Online "beyond" the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, parent company Take-Two has confirmed.
articles.body:
Rockstar Games plans to support GTA Online "beyond" the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 , parent company Take-Two has confirmed.

During a recent shareholders meeting (via ResetEra ), Take-Two said "we will continue to support GTA Online after GTA 6 release and beyond." Rockstar had already confirmed that GTA 6 is a single-player only game, so there won't be a multiplayer mode when the game comes out in November. As a result, if you want your online Grand Theft Auto fix, you'll have to divert your attention back to the original iteration of GTA Online.

Presumably there will be another iteration of GTA Online later down the line, but it's becoming increasingly unclear how and when it will be released. Will it be bundled with GTA 6 retroactively? Will it be a standalone game that players have to buy separately?

Twitch boss Dan Clancy, however, is convinced GTA 6 multiplayer will be released in 2027 . In a recent interview with Bloomberg , Clancy said he’d spoken with Rockstar about what the developer has up its sleeve. “We spent a lot of time talking with Rockstar about their plans, and also helping them think about how they can engage our creators,” Clancy said. “You are going to see this big bump with GTA 6, but then an even bigger one next year when they launch multiplayer.”

Meanwhile, during the shareholders meeting, Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick responded (via GamesRadar ) to a question about whether the plan for PC had been affected by console shortages, particularly the PS5 Pro.

"The strategy of the company is, over time, generally speaking, to launch for any platforms for which there's a meaningful audience," Zelnick replied, keeping his cards close to his chest. "But that isn't always the case, and certainly, if platforms were no longer viable, we could change that strategy.

"And I would note that the PC platform is becoming more and more important to our company over time."

Zelnick previously said that Rockstar has historically always released its games for consoles first , suggesting a PC version of GTA 6 may follow later. How much later? It's unclear, but GTA 5 remains a massively popular game on the platform.

Even More GTA 6 Screenshots from Rockstar Games

Ex-Rockstar Games producer John Ricchio stated in an interview earlier this year that the studio's continued decision to skip PC at launch wasn't one rooted in greed . Instead, it was a result of Rockstar wanting to optimize for consoles first and then scaling up for a PC version.

"It's always better to start with the constraints and then extend," said Ricchio. "Because shrinking is a lot harder than extending. It's way harder to make your game performant than it is to just be like 'Oh, we've got extra room? Cool, we can deoptimize or make things more shiny.'"

Could a PC version come alongside the next version of GTA Online? It doesn't seem out of the question if there's going to be a sizable gap. Either way, it's clear that Rockstar is pouring a lot of effort and focus into making GTA 6 the best single-player experience it can be without compromising other parts of the game, even if that means a staggered release of the long-term online money maker.

In related news, Rockstar Games announced Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album this morning . The soundtrack releases alongside the game on November 19 and features over 30 original songs from major mainstream artists. Six orignal songs from artists like Travis Scott, PinkPantheress, and Morgan Wallen are available to stream on Spotify right now.

articles.title: Brandon Sanderson Reflects on The Wheel of Time Cancellation and Being 'Loud Behind the Scenes'
articles.summary: Brandon Sanderson reflects on the cancellation of Prime Video's The Wheel of Time, saying he was "loud behind the scenes" about disliking the show's changes from the books.
articles.body:
Brandon Sanderson has reflected on the cancellation of Amazon's The Wheel of Time series in a recent interview with IGN , describing the show's abrupt ending as a "tragedy" while reiterating his frustrations with some of the changes made to Robert Jordan's books.

The Wheel of Time was cancelled by Prime Video in May 2025 after three seasons , bringing the adaptation to an end just as its third season had seemingly started to win back some of the fans who had been critical of its earlier departures from Jordan's novels.

At the time, Sanderson was openly critical of how the cancellation was handled. He said he had learned about it from the news after going two months without hearing anything from the production, and argued that the show's fanbase deserved better after what he considered its strongest season.

More than a year later, Sanderson's feelings haven't changed much, although his latest comments put more emphasis on the people left behind by the cancellation.

"It's a tragedy," Sanderson said when asked how he now reflects on the show. "In part for the cast and crew, whom I knew worked extremely hard, only to have their story end up unfinished."

Sanderson, who completed The Wheel of Time after Jordan's death using material and notes left by the original author, also singled out Rosamund Pike's performance as Moiraine as something he believes would be difficult to replace in another adaptation.

"I don't know if it would ever be possible to get a better Moiraine than Rosamund, for example," he said.

But while Sanderson has sympathy for the people who worked on the show, he still has significant reservations about the creative decisions made during its three-season run.

"At the same time, I wish I'd been able to persuade them to stick to the books in a few key aspects," he said.

That doesn't mean Sanderson believes adaptations have to follow their source material religiously. In fact, he was careful to make clear that he isn't opposed to changes when moving a story from one medium to another.

"I'm not one who thinks nothing can ever change in an adaptation," he said. "But there were alterations made here that led to an ever-widening gulf between Robert Jordan's vision and the show."

Sanderson believes there was ultimately a way for Amazon to make the changes it wanted while retaining more of what made Jordan's books distinctive.

"I feel there was a way to do what Amazon wanted and what the fans wanted, and maintain a little more clarity as to the themes of the books," he said.

Would Brandon Sanderson Return for Another Wheel of Time Adaptation?

Despite his frustrations with the Prime Video series, Sanderson hasn't ruled out working on another adaptation of The Wheel of Time in the future.

"If they want me!" he said when asked whether he would still be interested in being involved with future adaptations.

"They might not, as I was kind of loud behind the scenes about my dislike of some of these changes," he added.

Sanderson's involvement with the Amazon series was never as extensive as some fans might have hoped. While he was consulted during the show's development and production, he has previously spoken about feeling that his input was not meaningfully incorporated into the adaptation.

His relationship with the people who control the television and film rights is now effectively separate from his ongoing work with The Wheel of Time itself.

"I have an excellent relationship with Harriet and her team," Sanderson said, referring to Harriet McDougal, Jordan's widow and one of the key figures overseeing his literary legacy.

The Wheel of Time Season 3 Character Posters

"I'm publishing Wheel of Time leatherbound editions right now, and worked extensively with Harriet and Maria on perfecting those."

As for the television and film rights holders, Sanderson said: "I have not spoken to the tv/film rights holders in many years."

For now, there is no official indication that The Wheel of Time will return in another television or film adaptation. The Prime Video series concluded with its third season, and reports following its cancellation indicated that the show was not being actively shopped to another streaming service.

That leaves Sanderson's comments as something of a postmortem on an adaptation that came to an end before it could tell the complete story of Jordan's sprawling fantasy saga.

For fans, there is at least the possibility that The Wheel of Time could eventually get another chance on screen. Sanderson's comments suggest that, if it does, he would still be willing to have a seat at the table, provided someone actually wants him there.

articles.title: Activision Calls Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 'The Epic Conclusion,' Leaving Fans Wondering What's Next
articles.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is being advertised as the "epic conclusion," suggesting an end of an era for the franchise.
articles.body:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is being advertised as the "epic conclusion," suggesting an end of an era for the franchise.

In the social copy for the latest trailer for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , Activision stated that the game will be an "epic conclusion" for the Modern Warfare saga. It's unclear if this is the permanent end to the current Modern Warfare universe, or if this is just the end of the ongoing storyline that began back in 2019 with the rebooted Modern Warfare.

Although it's likely just a marketing buzz term, the branding comes at an interesting time. Earlier this week, Treyarch design director Kevin Drew stated that the studio was ready to "make something new and something that nobody's ever experienced before." The comments come as the studio waved goodbye to two back-to-back Black Ops games, with the most recent one being regarded as an underwhelming misfire for the series. The comments led fans to speculate that the Black Ops series may be coming to an end, or at least taking a break, allowing Treyarch to make its first new subfranchise in nearly 20 years.

Some fans are already waving goodbye to the current Modern Warfare series. "Reboot it again," joked one fan in a post on the Call of Duty subreddit . "They should do a COD Ghosts 2 or Infinite Warfare 2, both underrated campaigns," suggested another who may or may not be joking.

If Modern Warfare and Black Ops are truly coming to an end, it will be the first time the series hasn't had at least one existing sub-franchise in the rotation since the creation of Black Ops in 2010. Although we don't know what Sledgehammer Games is working on, it is likely a brand new subfranchise as Advanced Warfare and the studio's subsquent World War II games failed to catch on.

The original Modern Warfare series came to a close after just three games back in 2011. Although the team kicked around ideas for a fourth game back then, they didn't get very far and opted to create something new with Call of Duty: Ghosts.

After Ghosts and Infinity Ward's subsquent game, Infinite Warfare, failed to please fans, the studio went back to old faithful and rebooted Modern Warfare. 2019's effort is largely credited for pulling Call of Duty out of a multi-year rut where fans were beginning to lose faith in the series. It also gave birth to Warzone, the massively popular battle royale mode that has helped carry the series since launch.

During the Xbox Tokyo Game Show 2026 broadcast, Activision confirmed Death Stranding star Mads Mikkelsen is a major antagonist in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 . It's due out on PC and consoles - but not Xbox Game Pass - on October 23.
